questions.exact_problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,{v}^{2},\,4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$
questions.exact_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,0,\,-4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡u & 0 & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & 2v & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 2v & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡u & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8{v}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,-4{cos}^{2}⁡u,\,2v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.exact_solution:
Recall that for a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In part 4, we got the surface

$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [0,1],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(x),\,\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ),\,\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4x\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,4x\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂\theta }(x),\,\frac{∂}{∂\theta }(2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ),\,\frac{∂}{∂\theta }(2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 4x\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 4x\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}4x\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 4x\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4x\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & 2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 4x\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8{x}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +8{x}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ,\,-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨8{x}^{3}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ),\,-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨8{x}^{3},\,-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the corresponding norm is

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖ & =\sqrt{(8{x}^{3})^{2}+(-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64{x}^{6}+4{x}^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +4{x}^{4}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\sqrt{64{x}^{6}+4{x}^{4}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\sqrt{64{x}^{6}+4{x}^{4}} \\  & =2{x}^{2}\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,-v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v+uv\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩.\end{aligned}
